title: Differentiating a quadratic risk along a probability segment
source_anchor: Samplinglib original mathematical supplement v1, 2026-10-20; units[0] and its complete formula proof
target_statement: Let μ and ν be probability measures on a measurable parameter space W. Let Φ map W to a real Hilbert space H and be Bochner integrable under both laws, and let y be a fixed vector in H. Write m(ρ)=∫Φ dρ, R(ρ)=‖m(ρ)−y‖², and V(w)=2⟨m(μ)−y,Φ(w)⟩. For every 0≤t≤1, the actual positive measure ρₜ=(1−t)μ+tν is a probability, Φ is integrable under ρₜ, and its mean is the affine interpolation of the endpoint means. V is integrable under both endpoint laws. The right derivative of R(ρₜ) at zero is ∫V dν−∫V dμ. The exact remainder R(ν)−R(μ)−(∫V dν−∫V dμ) is ‖m(ν)−m(μ)‖², and is therefore nonnegative.
